content.text:
The recreation is complete. Here's a summary of what I built:

## Deliverables

**Source code** in `/workspace/recreation/src/` — original React 19 + TypeScript components:
- `editor/` — `useEditor.ts` (canvas/layer engine), `useActions.ts` (menu action router), `data.ts` (menu/tool/shortcut definitions), `types.ts`, `editor.css`
- `components/` — `MainMenu`, `TopBar`, `Toolbar`, `CanvasStage`, `RightSidebar`, `ColorPicker`, `Dialog`, `ShapesPopup`, `ShapePreview`, `Block`, `NumberInput`, `Icons`, `LogoBadge`

**Self-contained output** at `/workspace/recreation/output/index.html` (341 KB, all JS/CSS inlined via `vite-plugin-singlefile`, no external references).

## What the reference turned out to be

The site is **miniPaint** — a single-page browser image editor (not a multi-page site), so the loopback crawl terminates at one route (`/`). The complete product surface is a desktop-app-style workspace:

- **Menu bar** with 8 menus (File, Edit, View, Image, Layer, Effects, Tools, Help) and all nested submenus (Zoom, Guides, Flip, Language with 16 locales, Effects sub-filters, etc.), each with correct shortcut labels
- **Top attributes bar** that swaps controls per tool — brush/pencil (Size + Pressure), erase (Size/Circle/Strict), fill/magic-eraser (Power/Anti-aliasing/Contiguous), text (Font/Size/Fill/Stroke/Kerning/Leading), gradient, clone, blur, sharpen, bulge/pinch, animation, crop
